RAM Optimizer - test build
==========================

Requirements: Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit. No install needed.

Run it
------
1. Put RAMOptimizer.exe somewhere permanent first (e.g. Documents or
   C:\Tools). It registers itself to start with Windows from where it is,
   so if you move it later, just open it once from the new place.
2. Double-click RAMOptimizer.exe. If Windows says "Windows protected your
   PC" (the file isn't signed): More info > Run anyway.
3. It runs without administrator rights. To let game mode also clear the
   cache, turn on Settings > General > Admin mode (Windows asks once).

Where it lives
--------------
- Red button: hides the window; the app keeps running in the tray (the
  arrow near the clock). Left-click the tray icon to open it again;
  right-click for Optimize, Game mode and Quit.
- It starts with Windows by default, hidden in the tray. Turn that off in
  Settings (sliders icon, top right) > General.
- Opening the .exe again just shows the window of the running copy.
- It updates itself: a few hours after a new version is published (or on
  the next start) it downloads it, checks its signature and restarts into
  it. Never in the middle of a game. Settings > General shows the version.

What to try
-----------
- Numbers: compare with Task Manager > Performance > Memory.
- List button: your apps, biggest first. x closes an app (asks first);
  "Force quit" appears if the app ignores it.
- Chart button: usage for the last minute, hour or 24 hours, and which
  app was biggest at the peak. Hour/day fill in while the app runs.
- Ring button: auto-clear limit. Optimize: trims every background app.
- Bolt: game mode. Also turns on by itself when a game starts (Steam,
  Epic, Riot, Xbox, GOG, EA, Ubisoft folders, or anything fullscreen
  that isn't a browser or video player) and off when it closes.
- Settings > General: start with Windows, alerts, theme (System / Light /
  Dark), auto game mode, apps to close when gaming.
- Settings > Startup apps: what launches with Windows and how much RAM it
  uses now. Switch them off here (same as Task Manager's Startup tab).
- Settings > Check-up: RAM speed (XMP/EXPO), memory sticks, page file,
  memory compression.
- Alerts: a Windows notification when memory is about to run out, or an
  app keeps growing for an hour.

If something goes wrong
-----------------------
- Look for ram-optimizer.log next to the .exe and send it back.
- Run with demo data (touches nothing):  RAMOptimizer.exe --demo
- Quit from the tray menu restores every priority the app changed.
- To remove it fully: Settings > General > turn off "Start with Windows",
  quit from the tray, delete the .exe and %APPDATA%\RAM Optimizer.
